behavior_constraints: When all three flags (--run-provenance, --run-provenance-digest, --run-provenance-strict) are absent, every existing output remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
Empty value for --run-provenance or --run-provenance-digest exits 2 with exact stderr line and no output files created.
Missing parent directory for --run-provenance or --run-provenance-digest path exits 2 with exact stderr line and no output files created, checked before any output file is written.
--run-provenance-digest and --run-provenance-strict each require --run-provenance; missing it exits 2 with exact stderr line and no output files created.
--run-provenance-strict=true (bare or =true) rejects empty input dir (zero conforming shards) with exit 2 and exact stderr line; absent or =false keeps default behavior.

Validation order: empty-value check at parse time; requires-run-provenance check at parse time; parent-dir-exists check before any output file is written; empty-input-dir check for strict fires right after parent-dir check and before any output file is written.
Run-provenance file is pretty-printed JSON with 2-space indentation and a trailing newline, written via .tmp + rename after all other outputs (including every existing sidecar) are finalized.
Default top-level keys in exact order: schema_version, tool_version, flags, inputs_fingerprint, shard_count.
Strict mode extends key list in order with argv_sha256 and env_fingerprint immediately after shard_count; these keys appear ONLY when strict is explicitly true.
schema_version is fixed string 'eventq.run-provenance/v1'; tool_version is fixed string 'eventq/0.5.0'.
entities.summary: This round adds a standalone run-provenance sidecar (with optional digest and strict mode) to eventq ingest that records observed flag values and a sha256 input-shard fingerprint, gated by validation rules and emitting canonical JSON after all other outputs are finalized.

instruction_head:
# Run Provenance Sidecars

Add a standalone run-provenance sidecar so operators can see which
`eventq ingest` flag values were observed on the command line and how the set
of input shards was fingerprinted. The new sidecar avoids reconstructing that
information from logs, state files, manifests, and other sidecars.

`eventq ingest` now accepts exactly three new optional flags:
